How facebook is stealing billions of views.
Make sure to share this video on facebook. LOL.

The problem isn't that people are posting videos from one place on another place. That argument quickly becomes absurd - if "posting videos elsewhere steals my ad revenue", then what about saving a copy for yourself? Putting it on a disk and giving it to someone else? Playing it at a party? All of these things reduce the original author's ad revenue - just as if you see the video on Facebook, you're probably not going to head straight over to YouTube to see it on the author's "official" channel, if you see it anywhere else, you're probably not going to do that either, thus meaning you see it "for free", without contributing to the author's stream of revenue by watching advertisements.

The real problem I think is the business model itself, of making your money by making people watch advertisements when they see your content. This business model incentivizes a host of undesirable behaviors - since you get money from them watching ads on your content, it's in your best interests to make sure they see them, so it incentivizes making the blocking of ads difficult or nearly impossible. In addition, people can't watch your ads if they download the video, so it's also good for you if they can't, and have to look at it on the site every time they want to see it, so it's good for you if downloading a personal copy of the content in question is as difficult as possible. Similar arguments apply to things like derivative works (if a derivative gets more popular than the original, you don't get much from it).

A better model I think is the model of things like Kickstarter and Patreon - pay up front, or pay a constant amount to support the people you like. Pay-up-front models don't incentivize the same sort of nasty behaviors that pay-per-use models do, since they've already recouped their investment - no matter how many times people share it, they've already gotten the money it took to make it.
